0.comment: Mika: Huffman and the Schmidt Family
0.content:
Mika is the second son of the Schmidt family, a household of knights and travellers. His mother writes about local places and conditions; his father is a retired Knight of Favonius; his older brother Huffman is a serving knight who conducts safety patrols. When their parents went abroad, Huffman was meant to raise Mika, but he spent his days at work and his nights drinking with friends, so little Mika learned to look after himself and his brother. Their parents wrote home every week, and Mika traced their routes on a map. That is where his love of maps began. Huffman later told him the family map was outdated, taught him to fight, and joined their father in encouraging him to apply for the expedition: "You don't have to ask too much of yourself."

Lisa envies Huffman for having such a caring little brother. Kaeya wonders whether taking everything so seriously "runs in the Schmidts' blood". During the 3.1 event Huffman said he had been worried when Mika left with the Grand Master but now saw he had worried too much. Mika can't stand alcohol, "unlike my brother".

1.comment: Mika: Eula and the Reconnaissance Company
1.content:
The Reconnaissance Company scouts ahead of the Knights' main force, and Mika is its Front-Line Land Surveyor. Its captain, Eula, gave him far more tasks than the other recruits, which quickly made him adaptable. Once he got used to the way she expresses herself, they worked well together. He admires her mental strength: if people stared and whispered at him the way they do at her, he says, he could not leave his room. Eula expected him to last a few days like his predecessors. Instead he did everything without complaint and even volunteered to run her errands and help with communication, which led some knights to treat him as the leaders' official messenger.

Eula says the expedition left his personality unchanged but improved his abilities a lot, and that his unawareness of his own progress is a blind spot, "or perhaps he's just being humble". In 4.4 (limited event) Eula suggested the company stop at Wangshu Inn for Liyue food after an escort mission and noted that Mika cannot drink.

2.content:
Varka noticed Mika's teamwork during the recruitment trial and took him personally on the expedition as Front-Line Surveyor. He taught him combat every week, set him "homework", and advised him to avoid close combat and use a polearm with a crossbow. Mika calls him a strong leader who commands respect. Jean says Varka chose him less for his qualifications than for his hardworking, grounded nature. Varka jokes that since a lost man needs a mentor and a lost army needs a map, Mika is his mentor; Mika went pale at the joke.

Varka keeps using Mika as his courier. Mika carried the 3.1 Weinlesefest letter home from the far north. In the Nod-Krai period, at Favonius Keep, Varka handed him letters for Ratnik headquarters, for Nefer at the Curatorium of Secrets and for Mondstadt, with a last order: if danger appears, run; if you can't run fast enough, shout; if that isn't enough, do both. Mika says Varka "is always reliable when it comes to important business".

3.comment: Mika: Il Capitano and the Expedition Stand-off
3.content:
Deep in a dangerous restricted area in the north, the expedition's vanguard clashed with Fatui scouts, and both sides called for reinforcements until the commanders arrived. At night Mika saw a silent line of Fatui soldiers and, at their centre, a dark figure with glowing deep-blue eyes: the Harbinger Il Capitano. Mika knew he could not survive one half-hearted swing from him. Varka walked out to meet him, they talked briefly, and both forces withdrew. Varka joked that he would have liked a duel, and that the Captain knew a battle in a strange land would hurt both sides.

The experience taught Mika that strength alone is not enough; a knight must be able to handle any incident. He says he cannot imagine dealing with such an opponent: "Such powerful people are really on a level of their own." Varka's letter, which Mika read aloud in 3.1, says the Captain was not hostile and suggests this was because "Snezhnaya and we are in the same boat"; it adds that he had been ordered to Natlan.

4.content:
Mika's book-shaped surveying device was developed by Mika and Investigation Team technicians using Albedo's latest alchemical components. It holds a notebook with removable pages for making maps quickly. When elemental power is channelled into the carving on its back panel, a prism fires a "wavebeam" at a fan-shaped area. The time the beam takes to return gives the distance, and stronger pulses sketch the local terrain. All the other calculations must be done in the user's head, so only Mika can use it easily. Planned copies for other teams were shelved as spare parts for his. He never boasts about it, partly because that might make more work for Albedo.

Lohen once praised Mika for handling it "like it's nothing" and asked how he maintained it and whether he kept spare parts. Mika later noticed spare parts going missing and pages acting oddly, and began to suspect Lohen had been swapping in a fake and copying his intelligence. He never confirmed it.

5.content: Not long after joining the Reconnaissance Company, Mika went alone to update an outdated area, knocked a stone loose in some ruins and woke two Abyss Mages. Caught in their flames, he thought only of escaping to warn the others. A spinning spear and a burst of icy mist cleared the fire, and he fled, apologising loudly and promising to "knock before entering next time" so his seniors could fight them fairly. When the company came back, they found the mages' shields badly battered and saw the Vision glowing on his right wrist. That night's dinner was a celebration, and Mika seemed too stunned to understand why.

6.comment: Mika: Kaeya and the Recruitment Trial
6.content:
Because many Schmidts were already knights, the Knights made Mika's recruitment public and raised the bar. Lead examiner Kaeya set the tasks: hiking up Dragonspine in full armour with a heavy load, and mapping a monster-infested region without references. Mika helped the other two successful candidates along the way, treating them as future teammates. Kaeya gave him tips he didn't always understand, and Mika worried he was letting him down. Kaeya's teasing made him so nervous that he wrote Kaeya an apology letter.

Kaeya later enjoyed the rumour that Mika had beaten the Fatui, because it raised morale. In 3.1 he introduced Mika to the Traveler, and Mika fled within a few lines. In the Nod-Krai period Kaeya sent a bottle of cider with Mika for the Traveler, guessing they would miss it.

7.content: Mika calls Amber the most reliable vanguard. Front-Line Surveyors and Outriders both work ahead of the main force, and she taught him survival skills and how to look after his crossbow strings and arrows. Amber remembers that he answered "Yes, Commander!" to everything because she was close to Eula, and kept calling her "Ma'am" even after she explained she was an Outrider. In 3.1 she told the Traveler his shyness was a roundabout way of showing respect. They defended the walls together in Paralogism (5.6), and she sent the Traveler a message through him to Nod-Krai.

8.content: As a child, Mika studied geography books and practised drawing in the Knights' library. Lisa took a liking to the polite, hard-working boy, recommended books and told him his skills might qualify him for the Akademiya. Through the library he met Ella Musk, who needed a guide for a language-exchange trip into the wilds. On that first real expedition they reached their goal, but a mistake in Ella's word choice got them beaten up by hilichurls. Mika decided he needed to learn to protect himself. Lisa said in 3.1 that if anything were wrong, it would be written all over his face.

9.content: Albedo built Mika's survey equipment; during the Windblume's Breath event (3.5, limited) Sucrose, Albedo's assistant, called Mika an exceptional pathfinder who has taught surveying to others. Mika's attempts at artistic sketches reportedly left Albedo silent for a long time. Klee is Mika's friend and adventure companion. Her explosives keep reshaping the terrain, so he has to redraw his maps, and he thinks it is worth it. She told him about a plant that can relay sound, and he dreams of using it to report terrain from the front.

10.content:
Lohen is Vice Captain of the Fifth (Ranged) Company, which splits into squads to back up other companies, and he was a long-time member of Varka's expedition. He is around Mika's age. He checks every survey with Mika and does "armed recon" to fill the gaps, which means charging monster camps alone. Mika started leaving monster gathering points off the maps he handed him; Lohen read the truth on his face anyway. Mika admires his fighting spirit and the way he inspires his companions, but thinks they need teammates to rein them in. He also says Lohen's pranks are "not so bad" once you get used to them.

In 6.2 (limited event) Mika helped Lohen's old company adjust to new duties when some members returned to Mondstadt. Lohen later sent Tres to learn cartography from him. One of Mika's voice lines frets that their notebooks got switched and Lohen has run off to fight alone again: "If I were a captain too, then maybe he'd listen to me..."

11.content: In the limited-time Of Ballads and Brews event (3.1), Mika arrived back in Mondstadt carrying a letter from Varka, and Jean had him read it to the assembled Knights. It said the expedition was safe, writing "from the northernmost reaches of Teyvat". It mentioned an unhostile meeting with Il Capitano, who had since been ordered to Natlan, and sent festival wishes, ending with Varka's boast that there are ten captains but only one Grand Master ("His laugh, not mine," Mika added). Afterwards Mika barely managed a greeting to the Traveler before fleeing to report to Eula. Jean said Varka had ordered him back to the Reconnaissance Company.

12.content:
In Version 6.0 the Traveler ran into Mika shopping in Nasha Town, Nod-Krai. Jean had sent him to deliver the Knights' letters to Varka. He passed on her message that the Knights stand behind their Honorary Knight, gave the Traveler a bottle of cider from Kaeya, and passed along Amber's invitation to come home for Sweet Madame and steak. Varka had asked for Dandelion Wine; Jean told him to travel light, but Mika packed two bottles anyway so Varka wouldn't talk his ear off about it.

At Favonius Keep, Varka sent him on with letters for Ratnik headquarters, for Nefer at the Curatorium of Secrets and for Mondstadt. Back home, Mika read aloud Varka's detailed open letter about the battle against Rerir. By 6.4 Paimon was complaining that Varka had used Mika, Ineffa and Lohen as mail carriers, and Mika was hoping his maps would get the returning expedition home safely.

13.content: During the limited-time Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event (6.2), Mika helped run Dragonspine's International Cross Country Challenge. He had rescued "Mural Maniac", a Graffiti Alliance artist from Natlan's Masters of the Night-Wind, from Dragonspine's cold. Together they built the "Saury-Saury Scout", a survey drone that combines the core of a Sumeru Scouting Buddy (brought back by Amber) with a little saurian toy his Natlan friends gave him. Mika made the casing, his first development project. Hearing Natlanese tales of the Traveler's deeds made him so awed that he briefly called them "sir" or "ma'am". He resolved to seek new experiences rather than rely on diligence alone, and argued that machines multiply people's abilities rather than replace them.

14.content: In a limited-time event (6.5), Mika ran a surveying exchange in Starfell Valley. He taught Tres of the Ranged Company, sent by Lohen to learn cartography, with help from Elowen of the Reconnaissance Company. They designed a "Surveying and Searching" course that even a beginner could handle, with help from allied troops met at an earlier joint exercise. Tres calls him "Instructor Mika", and Paimon declared Tres a graduate of "Mika Academy". Mika's teaching motto: in surveying, "you're not the only person affected by the results." He found he learned from teaching too, and talked about taking a long holiday somewhere new.

15.content: At the limited-time Waterborne Poetry gala in Liyue (4.1), the Knights sent Mika and Noelle to keep order and set up the venue. He chose the site and drew up the layout, and he and Noelle each insisted the other take credit. When the Oceanid Callirhoe hesitated to see her old love, Old Finch of Springvale, Mika burst out that Grandpa Finch had encouraged him when he was learning to draw maps and still waits by the spring. Then he was mortified at himself. He knew of Oceanids only from Varka's stories and had thought they were local legend.

16.content: Mika heard about the Honorary Knight when he got back to Mondstadt. He feared that, like many powerful people, they might have a strict code and a temper, and was relieved to find them and Paimon kind. Now he wants to travel with them, survey the land for them and stop "dragging you down". He sends birthday letters with maps and food, suggests code words, and in the Serenitea Pot wants a craggy mountain to keep in shape. His 2026 letter hopes they might meet in Snezhnaya.

17.content: During the Paralogism crisis (5.6), when monsters stormed Mondstadt City during Albedo's trial, Mika and Amber cleared hilichurls from the city walls while the Knights and townspeople defended their homes. Albedo later revealed the trial had been planned for half a year to lure out an impostor. Canon does not say whether Mika was told beforehand.
